labels.note: Live report that something is broken; Max cannot diagnose so it hands over.
Plain ask for time; send the scheduling link, no person needed.
Negation rule: the cancel is explicitly disclaimed and nothing else is actionable.
Broken output in a live workflow; diagnosis belongs to a person.
Unambiguous request for time, reversible action, link only.
Negation rule: booking is explicitly deferred, so no book intent exists yet.
Data mismatch needing a verified answer; Max must never assert an unverifiable figure.
Bare day proposal is still a request for time; link is reversible either way.
Negation scopes to descoping only; 'quite the opposite' leaves a live scope signal.
Live outage on the client's own checkout; the relative is the reporter, not a third-party subject.
Booking ask with constraints; the grumble is about their own colleague, not dissatisfaction with the work.
Retraction of a prior scheduling instruction; nothing left to act on.
Failed payment flow plus a request for wording Max cannot commit to; no full card number so not lane D.
Direct booking ask; attendee list does not change the lane.
Negation rule: an explicit statement that nothing is being cancelled carries no cancel intent.
Forwarded but live blocker on the client's own system; relaying does not neutralise it.
Request for an additional session with a time preference; send the link.
Hypothetical outage carries no problem intent; the buried live question is a documented escalation-process one.
Reproducible failure report; diagnosis is off-limits to Max.
Booking ask; the topic being near a data issue does not change the intent.
Legal review of contract wording plus a timeline question; lane D overrides and silence beats helpfulness.
Idiom rule: 'site down' is an outage report, not agreement.
Request for a session; unambiguous and reversible.
Asks what a launch would require; that is scope, and the disclaimer does not make the question hypothetical.
Recurring bug plus explicit escalation language; both intents sit in lane C.
Booking ask; the sign-off thanks is not a separate social intent.
Asks for Max's preferred lead time, an opinion rather than a documented process answer.
Impossible state in live data; a person must investigate.
Request for a short slot; send the link.
Third-party rule: their supplier's invoice is not our money, and no action is requested.
Past/resolved rule: no live problem, just an acknowledgement, so react rather than reply.
Offering availability is a request for time; link is the safe reversible action.
Third-party rule: their dentist moved, our standup is untouched and they will attend.
Hedged wording still describes a live discrepancy; hedging does not make it hypothetical.
Request for an immediate call; scheduling link is the reversible response.
Third-party rule: another vendor's stale invites, no dissatisfaction with us and nothing to act on.
Terse but unambiguous outage report.
Proposes a new session next week; plain booking ask.
Third-party rule: their internal audit call moved and our QBR is explicitly untouched.
Error-code detail for a failed order; card last-four is not a card number, so lane D does not fire.
Unambiguous ask for time today.
Past/resolved rule: fixed on their side, so no live problem intent.
Live customer-facing defect; relayed by a colleague but still theirs.
Booking ask whose topic sits near a problem area; nearness is not intent.
Past/resolved rule: explicitly closed, nothing live and nothing to act on.
Failing load test with a technical question Max must not answer.
A standing constraint on an existing recurring slot reads as a reschedule, not a cancellation.
Past/resolved rule: asserts the item is closed; Max cannot verify either way, so nothing fires.
Recurrence of a known defect is live; the discount wording is topic, not a money ask.
Shifts an existing call; send the link.
Past/resolved rule: the planning work already happened and no scheduled call is explicitly cancelled.
Measured performance failure; a person must handle it.
Time shift on an existing call.
Idiom rule splits the two: outage is lane C, 'im down' is agreement; the safe intent is promoted to B.
Past/resolved rule: explicitly a false alarm with a cause found, so no live problem.
Shift request on today's call.
Billing question is lane C; the thanks stays actionable as a reaction and is promoted to B.
Accumulating failures plus a diagnosis question; Max must not confirm a cause.
Reschedule request on an existing call.
Idiom rule: 'dead in the water' is self-corrected to a delay, no outage and no ask.
Broken storefront behaviour; hand over.
Time shift on an existing call.
A stop instruction with no identifiable referent; uncertainty is about the intent itself, so hand over.
Reporting data that is provably wrong; Max cannot verify or explain it.
Reschedule request; reversible, send the link.
Self-clarified as an internal, non-production launch with no ask attached.
Live fulfilment defect with scale attached; hand over.
Same slot on a different day is a reschedule.
Politeness wraps a live status chase on open issues; Max cannot report on triage state.
Live checkout failure on a named platform.
Attendee conflict moves our call; the third party is inside our meeting, not outside it.
Politeness and a light jab still frame a genuine ask for time; the edge is not dissatisfaction with the work.
Recurring discrepancy with the prior explanation rejected; only a person can respond.
Day swap; the pleasantry is not a separate intent.
Scheduling driven by dissatisfaction: book it and flag it hard.
A fresh occurrence makes it live; Max cannot confirm a fix it has not verified.
Cancellation is act-and-notify: cancel, offer rebooking, post internally as a health signal.
Praise only; react, do not compose a reply.
Live defect with financial impact; the money wording is the consequence, not a billing ask.
Skipping a scheduled call is a cancellation: act and notify.
Understatement does not downgrade it; a payment outage is a live problem to hand over.
Past/resolved rule: explicitly not broken, correcting an earlier report.
Dropping out of a booked call is a cancellation on their side and a health signal worth posting.
Asks Max to guarantee how information is handled; Max makes no commitments, and it is not lawyers or PII so not lane D.
Customer-facing defect in live comms.
In a scheduling thread this cancels the call; act, offer rebooking, notify.
Office pleasantry; 'confidential' here is not legal or PII, so lane D does not fire.
Live error with a diagnosis question attached; Max must not attempt the diagnosis.
Cancellation of this week's call: act and notify.
The softener does not change the intent; 200 blocked orders is a live problem.
Reproducible inconsistency with a customer-visible balance.
Explicit cancellation; the absent colleague is the reason, not the subject.
No card number so not PII, and the billing item is already handled on their side with no ask.
Live pricing defect plus a request to confirm intended behaviour Max cannot verify.
Cancels today's call: act, offer rebooking, notify.
The final clause withdraws the request, so the negation resolves to no live booking intent.
Volume flag on a live data-integrity defect; buried in an update but still live.
Drops a scheduled call: cancel and post internally.
Corrected instruction is a live directive about release timing, which is commitment territory.
Resolved on their side, but the buried question asks for a root cause Max must not supply.
